top_choice_rationale: P002 (Melitz and Helpman, B012) is a single, well-defined mechanism: trade induces selection across heterogeneous firms, which reallocates resources and adds a channel for gains from trade. Melitz (2003) originated it, and Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to the exporting-versus-FDI choice. It has been tested on firm-level microdata for over two decades, and its core insight has not been overturned. Credit sits cleanly with two names, provided the citation names the selection and reallocation mechanism and leaves the Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum contributions and the functional-form-dependent welfare magnitudes to the Scientific Background. P001 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn, B022) is a very close second. Its question is first-order, its designs are transparent, and it has about a decade of open scrutiny. With the citation narrowed to the empirical evidence, the trio is a defensible attribution. I rank it below P002 only because the size and persistence of the China-shock effects are still being revised, and because of the task-framework credit outside the set and the thematic proximity to 2024. That ordering is a narrow judgement on common criteria and not a claim of deficiency. P000 is last because both proposals describe prize-level work with workable attribution.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for the credited names on P002 (Melitz, Helpman) or P001 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn). My collegial ties are to Boppart, Friberg and Krusell (co-authors and IIES colleagues), none of whom is a credited name on either proposal. I am also an explicit supporter of P002, so that support is not independent evidence of merit. Disclosed and not adjudicated.
